question: An 18-year-old man comes to the physician because of severe left shoulder pain after a basketball match. During the game, the patient sustained an injury to the posterior part of his outstretched arm after being blocked by a defender. Examination shows no gross deformity of the left shoulder. Palpation of the shoulder elicits mild tenderness. Internal rotation of the arm against resistance shows weakness. These findings are most specific for injury to which of the following muscles?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "18-year-old man with left shoulder pain" -> "injury during basketball match" -> "posterior arm injury" -> "mild tenderness on palpation" -> "weakness in internal rotation against resistance" -> "subscapularis muscle primarily responsible for internal rotation" -> "most specific for subscapularis injury" -> 85%

CHAIN: "18-year-old man with left shoulder pain" -> "sustained injury during sports" -> "posterior shoulder involvement" -> "internal rotation weakness noted" -> "subscapularis is the primary internal rotator" -> "indicates possible subscapularis injury" -> 80%

CHAIN: "18-year-old man with left shoulder pain" -> "injury mechanism suggests rotator cuff involvement" -> "internal rotation weakness" -> "subscapularis is involved in internal rotation" -> "less likely for supraspinatus or infraspinatus" -> "most specific for subscapularis" -> 90%

CHAIN: "18-year-old man with left shoulder pain" -> "posterior arm injury during basketball" -> "weakness in internal rotation" -> "subscapularis muscle is key for this action" -> "indicates subscapularis injury" -> 75%
analysis: The patient's symptoms, particularly the weakness during internal rotation against resistance, suggest an injury to the subscapularis muscle. The subscapularis is responsible for internal rotation of the arm, and weakness in this action is indicative of its involvement. Other muscles listed, such as the supraspinatus and infraspinatus, are more associated with abduction and external rotation, respectively.
